body:
**Claude finished @cmungall's task in 8m 24s** —— [View job](https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/actions/runs/42367470021)

---
### Review: PR #6196 — bacterial methionine cycle audit

- [x] Schema validation passes (recorded `just validate-all` PASS at science commit; CI still running)
- [x] All PMIDs verified as real (incl. the two 2026 ones)
- [x] Supporting text matches publication content (spot-checked verbatim)
- [ ] **GO terms correct and specific** — one over-reach in `THEMA/mtaD`
- [ ] **Review actions well-justified** — several rows carry quotes/reasons that don't support the claim
- [x] Core functions accurately identified
- [x] No over-annotation issues missed (MesD/MesB/MesX handling is exemplary)

This is a strong, carefully-hedged audit. Every GOA row is accounted for — per-gene `existing_annotations` counts match `*-goa.tsv` exactly (metH 27/27, metK 29/29, metE 17/17, mmuM 10/10, MYCS2 metH 12/12, THEMA ahcY 6/6, mtaD 8/8, …). All six `REMOVE`s are bare `GO:0005515` under the sanctioned protein-binding exception, with the real interaction (GroEL, UvrD, flavodoxin, DnaK) retained in prose rather than denied. The `pfs` changes correctly convert `MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED` → `MODIFY` + `GO:0006152` per the "correct but general is MODIFY" rule, and the `GO:0046124` downgrade to `UNDECIDED` on an honest ontology-scope reading is the right call. IBA rows follow the phylogeny-reading convention (no donor-count-as-strength, target self-evidence explicitly not called circular). The `proposed_molecular_function` + matching `proposed_new_terms` pattern for SIH hydrolase in `THEMA/ahcY` is exactly the documented mechanism.

The issues below are all localized evidence-attachment defects, not biology errors.

---

#### 🟡 IMPORTANT

**1. `ECOLI/metK` — metal- and ATP-binding rows cite quotes with no metal or ATP content**

[`metK-ai-review.yaml:16-52`](genes/ECOLI/metK/metK-ai-review.yaml#L16) — both `GO:0000287 magnesium ion binding` rows are supported only by PMID:10551856's *"Initially the sulfur of methionine displaces the intact tripolyphosphate chain (PPP(i)) from ATP…"*. That sentence never mentions magnesium or a metal. The correct quote is already sitting in this same file's `references` block at line 773: PMID:6251075 *"Both enzymatic activities require a divalent metal ion and are markedly stimulated by certain monovalent cations."* — and that abstract also carries the explicit Mg²⁺/Mn²⁺/Co²⁺ metal-nucleotide stereochemistry sentence. (The `GO:0030955 potassium` rows get this right, citing the Glu42/K⁺ quote.)

[`metK-ai-review.yaml:252-270`](genes/ECOLI/metK/metK-ai-review.yaml#L252) — `GO:0005524 ATP binding` is supported by PMID:7629176 *"The AdoMet synthetase mutants (i.e. MetK/C90A, MetK/C90S, and MetK/C240A) retained up to approximately 10% of wild type activity"*, a cysteine-mutant residual-activity result. Its `reason` is also verbatim copy-paste from the metal rows and ends "…exclusive physiological use of every metal active in vitro", a non-sequitur for ATP. PMID:6251075's AMP-PNP substitution sentence, or 10551856's own ATP clause, would both actually support the row. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20cmungall%2Faigr-methionine-cycle-taxon-audit%2C%20in%20genes%2FECOLI%2FmetK%2FmetK-ai-review.yaml%3A%20the%20two%20GO%3A0000287%20magnesium%20ion%20binding%20rows%20(lines%2016-52)%20cite%20PMID%3A10551856's%20tripolyphosphate%20quote%2C%20which%20contains%20no%20metal%20content.%20Replace%20supported_by%20with%20the%20PMID%3A6251075%20quote%20already%20present%20in%20the%20references%20block%3A%20%22Both%20enzymatic%20activities%20require%20a%20divalent%20metal%20ion%20and%20are%20markedly%20stimulated%20by%20certain%20monovalent%20cations.%22%20Also%20fix%20GO%3A0005524%20ATP%20binding%20(line%20252)%2C%20which%20cites%20a%20cysteine-mutant%20activity%20quote%20from%20PMID%3A7629176%20and%20whose%20reason%20text%20is%20copy-pasted%20from%20the%20metal%20rows%20(it%20ends%20'exclusive%20physiological%20use%20of%20every%20metal%20active%20in%20vitro'%2C%20which%20makes%20no%20sense%20for%20ATP).%20Keep%20quotes%20verbatim%20and%20re-run%20just%20validate%20ECOLI%20metK.&repo=ai4curation/ai-gene-review)

**2. `ECOLI/metH` — the cobalamin-*independent* half of PMID:8572314 is quoted to support cobalamin-dependent claims**

[`metH-ai-review.yaml:343-360`](genes/ECOLI/metH/metH-ai-review.yaml#L343) — `GO:0031419 cobalamin binding` is supported by *"We also report the extension of this assay method for use in activity measurements of cobalamin-independent methionine synthase."* That is the MetE half of the paper; it supports neither cobalamin binding nor MetH. The same abstract contains the right sentence: *"We report optimization of this reaction for assay of cobalamin-dependent methionine synthase to give an economical method for determining enzyme activity."* The same wrong-half quote is reused on `GO:0008705 methionine synthase activity` ([`:232-247`](genes/ECOLI/metH/metH-ai-review.yaml#L232)) and `GO:0071265` ([`:511-528`](genes/ECOLI/metH/metH-ai-review.yaml#L511)). This looks like a metE-side quote that leaked into metH. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20cmungall%2Faigr-methionine-cycle-taxon-audit%2C%20in%20genes%2FECOLI%2FmetH%2FmetH-ai-review.yaml%3A%20three%20rows%20(GO%3A0031419%20cobalamin%20binding%20at%20line%20343%2C%20GO%3A0008705%20at%20line%20232%2C%20GO%3A0071265%20at%20line%20511)%20cite%20PMID%3A8572314%20with%20the%20quote%20'We%20also%20report%20the%20extension%20of%20this%20assay%20method%20for%20use%20in%20activity%20measurements%20of%20cobalamin-independent%20methionine%20synthase.'%20That%20is%20the%20MetE%20half%20of%20the%20paper%20and%20does%20not%20support%20cobalamin-dependent%20MetH.%20Replace%20with%20the%20verbatim%20cobalamin-dependent%20sentence%20from%20the%20same%20cached%20abstract%3A%20'We%20report%20optimization%20of%20this%20reaction%20for%20assay%20of%20cobalamin-dependent%20methionine%20synthase%20to%20give%20an%20economical%20method%20for%20determining%20enzyme%20activity'.%20Re-run%20just%20validate%20ECOLI%20metH.&repo=ai4curation/ai-gene-review)

**3. `ECOLI/metH` — a pasted `reason` clause that does not justify its rows**

The sentence *"The cached abstract explicitly treats both enzyme types but does not resolve each folate glutamyl-chain length; the exact MetE substrate distinction is established by the independent full-text source"* appears on metH's cobalamin-binding ([`:350`](genes/ECOLI/metH/metH-ai-review.yaml#L350)), folate-cycle ([`:390`](genes/ECOLI/metH/metH-ai-review.yaml#L390)) and L-methionine-biosynthesis ([`:517`](genes/ECOLI/metH/metH-ai-review.yaml#L517)) rows. It is about *MetE's* folate donor and says nothing about any of those three claims. Per the skill's standard, `review.reason` must justify the chosen action for that row.

**4. `THEMA/mtaD` — two promiscuous activities asserted as co-equal replacement terms**

All five `MODIFY` rows ([`:24`, `:55`, `:82`, `:114`, `:155`](genes/THEMA/mtaD/mtaD-ai-review.yaml#L24)) propose the same four replacements: `GO:0050270` + `GO:0090614` + `GO:0004000 adenosine deaminase activity` + `GO:0090613 5'-deoxyadenosine deaminase activity`. But your own `23968233-scope.md` records the catalytic efficiencies: **SAH 1.1×10⁷, MTA 1.5×10⁶, 5′-deoxyadenosine 3.7×10⁴, adenosine 9.2×10³ M⁻¹s⁻¹** — the latter two are 300–1200× below SAH. The `reason` concedes they are "measured capacities, not established dominant physiological substrates", and `core_functions` keeps only SAH and MTA. So the action asserts four activities while the prose and core functions assert two. Per the promiscuous-activity tiers in `projects/ENZYME_SPECIFICITY.md`, state the judgement explicitly: adenosine and 5′-deoxyadenosine look like `KEEP_AS_NON_CORE`/`MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED` material (or `REMOVE`, if *T. maritima* has a dedicated adenosine deaminase — worth one QuickGO check), not refinements on par with the two real substrates.

---

#### 🔵 SUGGESTIONS

**5. PMID prefixes are stripped and run into adjacent words** — ~31 occurrences across the new reviews: `in17603473`, `Table1 of23968233`, `by17603473`, `Native33468593`, `E. coli8823155`, `primary17603473`, `ID16618097` (×8), `on35289639`. These render as mangled citations on the generated HTML pages; `PMID:17603473` reads correctly and stays greppable.

**6. `ECOLI/mmuM` `GO:0033528 S-methylmethionine cycle` ([`:176-205`](genes/ECOLI/mmuM/mmuM-ai-review.yaml#L176))** — the `reason`'s substantive point is that *E. coli* has no SAM→SMM methylation, i.e. the cycle as defined does not run in this organism and MmuM only catabolises exogenous SMM. That is a scope objection (`MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED`, or `MODIFY` toward an SMM-utilisation term) rather than "cannot decide". If the real blocker is the unadjudicated `PTN001843930` IBD rather than the biology, `UNDECIDED` is fine — but say that is the blocker, since the biology sentence currently argues for a stronger action.

**7. `PSEPK/metH` `GO:0005829` ([`:21-32`](genes/PSEPK/metH/metH-ai-review.yaml#L21))** — the `supporting_text` is byte-identical to the row's own `reason`, so it adds no independent support. `psepk-consultation/evidence.md` does contain a real result worth quoting instead (the 295/346-identity MesD alignment, the absent signal peptide / TM call). Noting this is an existing repo pattern (`hscB`, `iscS`, `hscA`), so it is not new here.

**8. `ECOLI/metK` `GO:0042802 → GO:0042803`** — the `reason` argues a dimer-of-dimers *tetramer* but lands on homodimerization activity. The explanation (homotetramerization is a BP, not an MF) is correct and you clearly checked it (`query-protein-homotetramerization.json`); one sentence naming that check in the `reason` would make the choice self-evident to a reader.

---

#### Verified, no action needed

- **PMID:42509803** (Biomolecules 2026, PMC13406329) and **PMID:42570567** (Microbiol Res 2026, doi 10.1016/j.micres.2026.128659) are real cached records, not hallucinations.
- Spot-checked quotes are verbatim: `Tm0172 catalyses the formation of homocysteine from either SIH`, `the ACIAD3524 mutant is auxotrophic for methionine`, `zinc is required for catalysis`, `redox cycling of the noncovalently bound cofactor NAD+`, `Not all enzymes, however, utilize SAM to catalyze methylation reactions.`
- **`GO:0008172` over `GO:0003871`/`GO:0008705` for MesD/MesB is the right call** — the donor is unidentified, so the generic S-methyltransferase parent is the honest term, and `MODIFY`-as-generalization is sanctioned for a wrong-donor specific term. The single `NEW` (cbdbA481, IDA) is a purified untagged protein with no-enzyme/no-homocysteine/crude-extract negative controls and LC-MS product confirmation — well above the `NEW` bar.
- **MesX gets no activity term and `existing_annotations: []`** with the DUF1852 prediction kept as a hypothesis in `findings`. Exactly right.
- **MYCS2 metE zinc** rests on `HAMAP-Rule:MF_00172` / `PIRSR000382-2`, both vetted UniRule systems — not ARBA.
- `A0R6Q9`/`Q88JF1`/`Q6F6Z8` reassignments are backed by the recorded 295/346-identity alignment and the linked MesX locus, not by name inheritance.
- Post-science commits (`952da72d4`, `21996f473`) touch only project metadata, so the recorded `validate-all` PASS at `125cfcb38` still covers the curated content.

Issues 1–4 are concrete and fixable now (the correct quotes for 1 and 2 are already in the respective files), so I'm requesting changes rather than deferring. The biology and the module design are sound.
 · branch [`cmungall/aigr-methionine-cycle-taxon-audit`](https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/tree/cmungall/aigr-methionine-cycle-taxon-audit)
